title: MCP (Model Context Protocol): how agents reach tools, and where you can stop them
summary: The control paths, commands, licensing statements and documented limitations are supported by Microsoft's pages. The deterministic pre-check flags reflect formatting or placeholder differences rather than incorrect controls.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls; What to check
claims.claim: Tenant-wide MCP server blocking is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools, and then select the Registry tab. ... Select an MCP server from the list to open its overview pane. ... Select Block to restrict the server across your organization

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls; What to check
claims.claim: Individual tool control is at Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Tools > Enabled / Disabled toggle > Save.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools, and then select the Registry tab. ... Select the Tools tab. The list shows every tool the server exposes, along with its description and an Enabled or Disabled toggle. ... Select Save to apply your changes

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls; What to check
claims.claim: Requested MCP server registrations are reviewed at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Requests (preview).
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools, and then select the Requests (preview) tab.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; What it is; Governance controls; What to check
claims.claim: Publisher-type availability for agents, plugins, connectors and MCP servers is at Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access.
claims.quote: Agent and plugin access controls which types of agents and plugins, including connectors and MCP servers, are available in your organization. ... go to Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access.

claims.where: controls[4].ui; What it is; Governance controls; What to check
claims.claim: Tenant user access for agents and plugins, including MCP servers and connectors, is at Agents > Settings > User access.
claims.quote: Plugins include tools, MCP servers, connectors, skills, and other AI artifacts. ... Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins.

claims.where: controls[5].ui; What it is; Governance controls
claims.claim: Federated connectors can be enabled or disabled under Copilot > Connectors > Your connections and staged through Staged rollout > Add staging.
claims.quote: Enable / Disable | Copilot > Connectors > Your connections ... Limit a connector to specific users or Microsoft Entra ID groups by choosing Add staging in the Staged rollout column.

claims.where: controls[6].ui; Governance controls; What to check
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy is reached through Agents > Tools > Registry > Work IQ MCP > Policy, when that tab is available.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools. ... In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP. ... On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: The single-environment advanced connector policy UI is at Power Platform admin center > Security > Data and privacy > Advanced connector policies.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Security. ... In the Security pane, select Data and privacy. ... Select Advanced connector policies.

claims.claim: POST /governance/ruleBasedPolicies?api-version=2024-10-01 creates an advanced connector policy before assignment.
claims.quote:
All examples in the article use API version 2024-10-01. ... $policy = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post `
    -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/governance/ruleBasedPolicies?api-version=$apiVersion"

claims.claim: POST /governance/ruleBasedPolicies/<policyId>/environmentGroups/<environmentGroupId>/assignments?api-version=2024-10-01 with {} assigns the policy to the group.
claims.quote:
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post `
    -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/governance/ruleBasedPolicies/$($policy.id)/environmentGroups/$environmentGroupId/assignments?api-version=$apiVersion" `
    -Headers $headers -ContentType "application/json" -Body "{}"

claims.claim: Classic data policy creation is at Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > + New Policy.
claims.quote: Select Security in the navigation pane. ... In the Security pane, under Settings, select Data and privacy. ... In the Data protection and privacy screen, select the Data policy section. Select + New Policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell provides New-DlpPolicy -DisplayName <name> -EnvironmentType <type> [-Environments <environments>] to create a data policy.
claims.quote:
Module: Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell Module ... New-DlpPolicy
    -DisplayName <String>
    -EnvironmentType <String>
    [-DefaultConnectorClassification <String>]
    [-Environments <Object>]

claims.where: controls[9].ui; What it is; Governance controls; What to check
claims.claim: Dataverse MCP client configuration is under Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol > Advanced Settings.
claims.quote: Select Manage > Environments. ... Select the Environment Name ... select Settings. Under Settings, select Product > Features. Scroll down to locate Dataverse Model Context Protocol ... Select Advanced Settings.

claims.claim: A PowerShell, Graph or REST equivalent of the registry MCP server Block action is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: MCP server block tool enabled approve requests admin API; MCP block Tools Graph beta Agent 365. Read manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers and develop-mcp; no registry blocking API found. Graph's Enterprise MCP service-principal disable is a different control.

claims.claim: A PowerShell, Graph or REST equivalent of registry individual-tool toggles is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: MCP server block tool enabled approve requests admin API; MCP block Tools Graph beta Agent 365. Opened manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers and develop-mcp; read Azure API Management Agent 365 search excerpts. No equivalent registry tool-toggle endpoint found.

claims.claim: Automation for approving MCP registration requests is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: MCP approval API Agent 365 requests; MCP approve Graph API registry. Opened develop-mcp and manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers. The CLI explicitly removed approve; results document admin-center approval, not an approval endpoint.

claims.claim: Automation for Agent and plugin access publisher-type settings is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent and plugin access User access PowerShell Graph API settings; User access Agent and plugin access Graph beta. Opened agent-settings and manage-federated-connectors; results give UI procedures but no API for this publisher-type setting.

claims.claim: Automation for the tenant-wide Agents > Settings > User access setting is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent and plugin access User access PowerShell Graph API settings; User access Agent and plugin access Graph beta. Opened agent-settings and manage-federated-connectors; no equivalent tenant User access API found.

claims.claim: Automation for federated connector enablement and staged rollout is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: federated connectors enable disable staged rollout API PowerShell. Opened federated-connectors-overview and manage-federated-connectors; read set-up-custom-federated-connectors excerpts. No equivalent API found; Entra authentication staged rollout is unrelated.

claims.claim: Automation for Work IQ MCP tenant policy is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP tenant policy configure API PowerShell Graph; Work IQ MCP policy API configure; Work IQ MCP policy PowerShell. Opened policy-governance-mcp; searched results describe policy payload concepts but supply no configuration endpoint or cmdlet.

claims.claim: Unblock restores access to a previously blocked MCP server.
claims.quote: Select Block to restrict the server across your organization, or Unblock to restore access to a previously blocked server.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Agent 365 service description lists tenant-wide tool access control as not included with Microsoft 365 plans and requiring Microsoft 365 E7 / G7 or Agent 365.
claims.quote: Included with Microsoft 365 Enterprise, Business, Education, and Front Line Worker plans | Requires Microsoft 365 E7 / G7 or Agent 365 ... Control which tools (including Microsoft MCP servers) agents can access tenant-wide | Microsoft 365 Admin Center | No | Yes | Yes

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risks and limits; Governance controls
claims.claim: Registry tool-level control is rolling out and supports only specific MCP server types.
claims.quote: Tool-level granular control is rolling out to tenants and supports only specific types of MCP servers registered on Agent 365.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Tool-level control in the registry is limited
claims.claim: In the registry, a server without tool discovery can only be controlled through whole-server blocking.
claims.quote: If an MCP server doesn't support tool discovery ... individual tools aren't available to manage. In this case, use Block or allow an MCP server to control the entire server instead.

claims.claim: Bring-your-own MCP server registration is in preview.
claims.quote: This feature is in preview.

claims.claim: The Agent 365 CLI reference instead points to Requested Agents for pending requests.
claims.quote: Tenant administrators now perform server approval and blocking in the Microsoft admin center — pending requests are reviewed on the Requested Agents page.

claims.claim: Managing federated connectors requires Global Administrator or Search Administrator.
claims.quote: To manage federated connectors, you need one of the following administrator roles: Global Administrator; Search Administrator

claims.claim: All users is the default User access value.
claims.quote: All users - This option is the default.

claims.claim: User access offers All users, No users and Specific users or groups.
claims.quote: The setting has three options: All users ... No users ... Specific users or groups

claims.claim: Federated connector staging cannot extend beyond User access.
claims.quote: Staging can't extend beyond the users allowed by User access.

claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.where: controls[7].note; Risks and limits; Governance controls
claims.claim: Advanced connector policies support MCP server-level blocking but not granular individual MCP tool control.
claims.quote: As of now, granular control over individual MCP tools (endpoints and actions) within an MCP server isn't available. Blocking the entire MCP server is supported.

claims.where: controls[8].note; What it is; Governance controls; What to check
claims.claim: Power Platform connector blocking also blocks tools in connected MCP servers that rely on those connectors.
claims.quote: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers, which rely on Power Platform connectors for connectivity.

claims.claim: The Copilot Studio client for Dataverse MCP is enabled by default.
claims.quote: By default, the Microsoft Copilot Studio client for Dataverse MCP is enabled for all environments.

claims.where: controls[9].note; Governance controls; What to check
claims.claim: Additional Dataverse MCP clients must be enabled before use.
claims.quote: You must enable the additional clients in the Power Platform admin center before you can connect to the client.

claims.claim: The allowedmcpclients API changes individual client records rather than the environment-wide MCP switch.
claims.quote: An MCP client that is allowed to talk to MCP endpoint ... Primary key: allowedmcpclientid ... isenabled | Edm.Boolean | Display name: Is Enabled

claims.claim: Model Context Protocol lets Copilot Studio agents connect to external knowledge servers, data sources and tools.
claims.quote: You can extend your agent with tools by using Model Context Protocol (MCP). ... Model Context Protocol (MCP) helps you connect to existing knowledge servers and data sources directly within Copilot Studio.

claims.quote: Each tool or resource that a connected MCP server publishes is automatically available for use in Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio agents can act as clients accessing MCP server content.
claims.quote: A single MCP server can integrate and manage multiple tools and resources. Copilot Studio agents can access each tool.

claims.quote: Resources: File-like data that an agent can read for more context, such as API responses or file contents

claims.claim: MCP tools are functions a language model can call to perform an action.
claims.quote: Tools: Functions that a language model can call to perform an action

claims.claim: MCP prompts are predefined templates.
claims.quote: Prompts: Predefined prompt templates to accomplish specific tasks

claims.claim: Copilot Studio currently supports MCP tools and resources.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio currently supports MCP tools and resources.

claims.claim: The MCP server supplies tool names, descriptions, inputs and outputs.
claims.quote: The server provides the name, description, inputs, and outputs.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio dynamically reflects server-side changes to tools and resources.
claims.quote: When you update or remove tools and resources on the MCP server, Copilot Studio dynamically reflects these changes.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio's standard-harness MCP guidance requires generative orchestration.
claims.quote: This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness. ... You must turn on generative orchestration to use MCP.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio supports the Streamable MCP transport.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio supports the Streamable transport type.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio no longer supports SSE for MCP after August 2025.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio no longer supports SSE for MCP after August 2025.

claims.where: What it is: governance table; What to check
claims.claim: Advanced connector policies govern MCP server use within Power Platform, including Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: MCP servers are special connector endpoints that expose MCP-enabled APIs and tooling capabilities within Power Platform. ... Until design-time support is available in a given maker portal, ACP operates as a runtime-only enforcement for that workload.

claims.claim: Work IQ offers a remote MCP server.
claims.quote: Work IQ API endpoints include A2A, a remote MCP server, and a REST API.

claims.claim: Federated connectors can create, update or delete source-system data on the user's behalf when the connector provides those tools.
claims.quote: Where a connector provides the tools, Copilot can also create, update, or delete data in the connected system on the user's behalf.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP provides tools for querying records.
claims.quote: The Dataverse MCP server provides tools for common data operations such as querying records, creating and updating rows, and describing table schemas.

claims.quote: The Dataverse MCP server provides tools for common data operations such as querying records, creating and updating rows, and describing table schemas.

claims.quote: Federated connectors are read-only; they can search and fetch content but can't write data back.

claims.claim: That general overview also announces write actions starting early October 2026.
claims.quote: Write actions will be available starting early October 2026.

claims.claim: Plugin package-level actions are not separate controls for every included component.
claims.quote: These package-level actions aren't separate controls for each included component.

claims.claim: No licence or meter for the MCP protocol itself is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Model Context Protocol MCP protocol license pricing meter. Opened agent-extend-action-mcp, Agent 365 service description, billing-credit-overview, Work IQ overview and Dataverse MCP FAQ. Results document product/server charges, not a protocol licence or protocol meter.

claims.claim: For agents on the Microsoft Copilot harness, tools including MCPs consume Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: Work IQ API usage is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing.
claims.quote: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP is available through usage-based billing.
claims.quote: Work IQ API endpoints include A2A, a remote MCP server, and a REST API. Usage is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.

claims.claim: The documented start date for charging external-agent access to Dataverse MCP tools is 15 December 2025.
claims.quote: Starting December 15, 2025, Dataverse MCP tools are charged when accessed by AI agents created outside of Microsoft Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP tools are charged when accessed by AI agents created outside Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Dataverse MCP tools are charged when accessed by AI agents created outside of Microsoft Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: Qualifying Dynamics 365 Premium licences or a Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription licence exempt access to Dynamics 365 data from those charges.
claims.quote: If you have qualifying Dynamics 365 Premium licenses or a Microsoft 365 Copilot User Subscription License (USL), you aren't charged for accessing Dynamics 365 data.

claims.claim: A user needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence to see a federated connector.
claims.quote: A user sees a federated connector in Copilot only when all of the following are true: ... The user has a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.where: Risks and limits: An advanced connector policy is a strict allowlist
claims.claim: Advanced connector policies block connectors not explicitly allowed.
claims.quote: ACP enforces a strict allowlist ... every connector that isn't explicitly allowed is blocked.

claims.where: Risks and limits: An advanced connector policy is a strict allowlist
claims.claim: The allowlist is enforced when saved for a single environment or published for an environment group.
claims.quote: ACP enforces a strict allowlist as soon as you save it (single environment) or publish it (environment group)

claims.claim: Advanced connector policies do not yet support custom connectors.
claims.quote: Custom connectors and HTTP connectors aren't yet supported.

claims.claim: Advanced connector policies do not yet support HTTP connectors.
claims.quote: Custom connectors and HTTP connectors aren't yet supported.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Blocking at the wrong level
claims.claim: MCP server blocking is a separate component-level action whose effects on dependent plugins and linked connectors depend on the management route.
claims.quote: Blocking an MCP server is a separate component-level action; effects on dependent plugins and linked connectors depend on the applicable management route.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Blocking at the wrong level
claims.claim: Blocking a plugin leaves its associated MCP servers available to other plugins.
claims.quote: Blocking a plugin prevents users from accessing the plugin and any agents that depend on it. Associated MCP servers and connectors remain available to other plugins.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio makes users responsible for tools and resources accessed from non-Microsoft MCP servers.
claims.quote: When you connect to a non-Microsoft product, including an external MCP server, you're responsible for the tools and resources you access from within Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: Data processed by non-Microsoft services is not subject to Microsoft agreements.
claims.quote: Data processed by non-Microsoft services isn't subject to Microsoft agreements.
